content: The overview page serves as a concise summary of all the microchapters within a given topic. It highlights the main subtitles of the page and provides a brief overview of the content within each microchapter. This page is typically created last and is designed to summarize the critical aspects of the disease for a quick reference. For an example of an overview page on pericarditis, refer to the provided link. The goal is to present the most essential information for a quick understanding of the disease. The structure and extent of the overview depend on the complexity of the disease being described. The Overview section provides a general summary of the disease. It should include the name of the disease in the first sentence and summarize the key points of all subsequent sections. This section should avoid synonyms or keywords, as these are listed elsewhere on the page. It is written at a level suitable for medical students or interns. For an example of an overview section, refer to the provided link. The Historical Perspective section discusses the initial discovery of the disease, significant outbreaks or events associated with it, and the early diagnostic and therapeutic advancements. The name of the disease should be mentioned in the first sentence. This section provides a concise description of landmark discoveries and is ideally written after the main historical perspective microchapter. It may mirror the overview seen in the historical perspective microchapter. For templates and examples, refer to the provided link. The Classification section outlines how the disease is categorized, which varies depending on the type of disease. For instance, cancers may be classified by stage and grade, while drug allergies may be classified by the type of drug reaction. The name of the disease should be included in the first sentence. This section provides a brief description of the classification system and is ideally written after the main classification microchapter. It may replicate the overview seen in the classification microchapter. For templates and examples, refer to the provided link. The Pathophysiology section explains the biological and physical manifestations of the disease as they relate to underlying abnormalities and physiological disturbances. The name of the disease should be included in the first sentence. This section provides a concise description of the disease process and is ideally written after the main pathophysiology microchapter. It may mirror the overview seen in the pathophysiology microchapter. For templates and examples, refer to the provided link. The Causes section summarizes the primary causes of the disease. It is ideally written after the main causes microchapter to summarize the key points. This section may replicate the overview found in the main causes microchapter. For templates and examples of causes (non-microbiology and microbiology), refer to the provided links. The Differentiating [Disease Name] from Other Conditions section provides a brief description of the main diseases that need to be distinguished from the disease being described. This section is ideally written after the main microchapter and may replicate the overview found in the main differentiating disease from other conditions microchapter. For templates and examples, refer to the provided link. The Epidemiology and Demographics section studies the causes, distribution, and control of the disease in populations. Demographics include objective characteristics such as age, marital status, family size, racial origin, prior disease, religion, income, and education, and their relationship to the disease. The name of the disease should be included in the first sentence. This section outlines the risk factors most strongly associated with the disease and is ideally written after the main epidemiology and demographics microchapter. It may replicate the overview found in the main epidemiology and demographics microchapter. For templates and examples, refer to the provided link. The Natural History, Complications, and Prognosis section describes the progression of the disease without treatment, the negative consequences of the disease and its treatment, and the expected outcomes. The name of the disease should be included in the first sentence. This section is ideally written after the main microchapter to summarize the key points and may replicate the overview seen in the natural history, complications, and prognosis microchapter. For templates and examples, refer to the provided link. The Diagnosis section details the most important signs, symptoms, tests, and studies that lead to the diagnosis of the disease. The name of the disease should be included in the first sentence. This section is ideally written after the main diagnosis microchapters to summarize the key points. The History and Symptoms section describes the key aspects of the patient’s history and symptoms that support or exclude the diagnosis of the disease. The name of the disease should be included in the first sentence. This section may replicate the overview found in the history and symptoms page. For templates and examples, refer to the provided link. The Physical Examination section outlines the main physical examination findings that support or exclude the diagnosis of the disease. The name of the disease should be included in the first sentence. This section may replicate the overview found in the physical examination page. For templates and examples, refer to the provided link. The Laboratory Findings section lists the main laboratory studies that support or exclude the diagnosis of the disease. The name of the disease should be included in the first sentence. This section may replicate the overview found in the laboratory findings page. For templates and examples, refer to the provided link. The Electrocardiogram section describes EKG findings relevant to the diagnosis of the disease. This section may replicate the overview found in the electrocardiogram page. For templates and examples, refer to the provided link. The Chest X-Ray section describes chest x-ray findings relevant to the disease. This section may replicate the overview found in the chest x-ray page. For templates and examples, refer to the provided link. The CT Scan section describes CT findings relevant to the disease. This section may replicate the overview found in the CT page. For templates and examples, refer to the provided link. The Echocardiography or Ultrasound section describes echocardiography or ultrasound findings relevant to the disease. This section may replicate the overview found in the echocardiography and ultrasound page. For templates and examples, refer to the provided link. The Other Imaging Findings section lists the most important diagnostic studies, including imaging, that support or exclude the diagnosis of the disease. Any gold standard studies should be named here, and the name of the disease should be included in the first sentence. For templates and examples, refer to the provided link. The Treatment section describes the most commonly used methods for treating the disease. The name of the disease should be included in the first sentence. This section is ideally written after the main treatment microchapter to summarize the key points and may replicate the overview found in the main treatment microchapter. The Medical Therapy section describes all non-surgical therapies provided for the patient. The name of the disease should be included in the first sentence, followed by the indication for treatment and the name of the therapy. For templates and examples, refer to the provided link. The Surgery section describes all surgical and therapeutic procedures provided for the patient. The name of the disease should be included in the first sentence, followed by the indication for surgical management and the name of the surgery. For templates and examples, refer to the provided link. The Prevention section outlines strategies to prevent the occurrence of the disease. Prevention may be primary (preventing disease occurrence), secondary (early diagnosis and treatment), tertiary (reducing the negative impact of existing disease), or quaternary (avoiding unnecessary interventions). At least primary and secondary prevention are usually discussed. The name of the disease should be included in the first sentence, and the availability or lack of a vaccine should be clearly stated. Other prevention strategies should be outlined and classified. For templates and examples, refer to the provided link.
